title: European Commission allocates 22.5 million euros in additional humanitarian aid to Yemen
excerpt: The funding addresses the consequences of renewed conflict escalation and the critical needs of 22.3 million people in Yemen.
bodyHtml:
The European Commission announced on October 23, 2026, that it is providing 22.5 million euros in humanitarian aid to Yemen. This allocation is in addition to 87.5 million euros previously provided for 2026.

The funding is intended to address the consequences of renewed conflict escalation and the needs of millions of people. According to the European Commission, 22.3 million people in Yemen currently require humanitarian assistance and protection. Recent military escalation has resulted in the displacement of nearly 230,000 people in recent weeks.

The aid will focus on food security, nutrition, health, water, sanitation, and hygiene. The European Commission stated that 5.2 million people are internally displaced in the country, while over 2.2 million children under five suffer from acute malnutrition.
